lede: Tulsa carries the stronger underlying team rating — -0.2 against -5.6, a 5.4-point separation on a neutral field before home advantage, travel or rest.
EdgeDesk makes it Sam Houston +7.0 before any sportsbook number is consulted, with Tulsa winning 68% of simulations.
The position-group comparison shows where the separation comes from: the widest measured gap is secondary, where Tulsa leads Sam Houston by 84 places nationally.
Data confidence on this matchup is 41% — enough to publish, not enough to treat the exact margin as settled.

underdog.heading: Why Sam Houston can keep it close
bullets: Playing at Sam Houston is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
The outcome range is 15.5 points wide at one sigma — p10 -31.0 to p90 +14.0 for Sam Houston, so a projection of -7.0 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 6%.
60% of the model’s own input contract was empty for this game — no starter, injury or per-player talent context reached it, so the number leans on team strength more than it should.
